source_user: A long-context workload intermittently hits OOM after several concurrent requests. Give a prioritized diagnosis and mitigations. Scenario variant 273: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure per-request KV growth and allocator fragmentation; check max sequence and batch; inspect active sequences; test paged/prefix cache, admission control, quantization, and context limits.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: GPU model and capacity, runtime and allocator versions, precision, parallelism, context limit, batching policy, cache implementation, and request-length/arrival distributions are unspecified; record them before interpreting the event. Treat intermittency as an observation, not proof of one cause. Preserve the failing seed and request-arrival trace plus a crash-free baseline.

Prioritized diagnosis: for every request and device, timestamp admission, prefill, decode, eviction, and failure. Record prompt and generated-token lengths, active sequences, batch membership, configured and observed maximum sequence length, KV pages/bytes and bytes per token, allocated versus reserved memory, largest free block/fragmentation, weights, activations, workspaces, CUDA/NCCL allocations, and cache-page ownership. First rule out one request exceeding context/max-position limits or an incorrect token-length estimate; next check concurrent long sequences, continuous-batching growth, anomalous KV growth, stale/leaked pages, allocator fragmentation, temporary workspace peaks, and replicated/topology-dependent allocations.

Falsifiable hypothesis: concurrent KV growth exhausts usable per-device headroom, with fragmentation amplifying the peak. Replay the same seeded trace while holding software and model fixed, and compare baseline with admission caps of 1/2/4/... and lower context caps. Measure OOM rate, peak allocated/reserved memory, KV bytes per live token, largest free block, active sequences, latency, and completed-token correctness over repeated trials. The hypothesis is supported only if reducing live-token demand lowers OOMs and the memory trace approaches the predicted KV slope; it is weakened if OOM occurs at similar KV and fragmentation levels or only with a particular workspace/topology. Confounders include changed request order, warmup, allocator state, CUDA graph/workspace selection, driver/runtime differences, hidden replicas, thermal throttling, and host-side admission delays.

Mitigate in stages: enforce per-request context and output limits; reserve headroom and admission-control by predicted KV demand; cap active sequences/batch tokens; fix cache ownership/eviction and use paged KV or prefix caching only after verifying isolation and invalidation; consider lower KV precision or weight quantization only with accuracy checks. Keep a known-good conservative configuration, monitor OOM rate, memory headroom, latency SLOs, and task correctness, and roll back any change that causes errors, cache leakage, quality regression, or SLO breach. Do not claim a root cause without the measurements.

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 25: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: framework and NCCL versions, launcher, host count, rank/world-size mapping, GPU model, topology, network fabric, interface names, container privileges, and timeout settings are unspecified; capture them rather than inferring platform facts. A hang can be rendezvous, visibility, topology, transport, or an earlier rank failure. Preserve logs from every rank with timestamps and do not immediately increase timeouts or retry indefinitely.

Prioritized diagnosis: log each rank's PID, hostname, local/global rank, world size, visible-device list, selected backend/interface, rendezvous endpoint, and the last completed initialization barrier. Verify that every expected rank starts exactly once, receives the same world size and rendezvous settings, reaches the same process-group call, and can connect to the rendezvous address. Check GPU visibility and exclusive ownership, device-to-rank mapping, peer access, topology, host clocks, firewall/ports, and NIC selection. Run a minimal deterministic all-reduce with a small tensor and explicit timeout, first on one node, then a reduced world, then the full world; collect per-rank success/failure and elapsed time.

Falsifiable hypothesis: the full-world hang is caused by a rank-specific rendezvous or selected-interface/transport path that cannot communicate, rather than by the collective algorithm itself. Hold versions and rank mapping fixed; compare single-node, reduced-world, and full-world runs while explicitly selecting the candidate interface and recording connection attempts, NCCL debug logs, topology, and timeout location. The hypothesis is supported if the first failing rank/path is stable and the minimal all-reduce succeeds when that interface or world-size condition is removed; it is weakened if all ranks reach the collective and the failure persists across interfaces and topologies. Confounders include an earlier process crash, stale rendezvous state, duplicate rank, mismatched environment variables, GPU reset, port collisions, asymmetric container networking, firewall policy, and misleading timeout symptoms.

Mitigate only after localization: correct rank/world-size/rendezvous configuration and stale-job cleanup; make GPU visibility and rank mapping explicit; select a verified interface and compatible transport; validate peer access/topology and required ports; use a bounded timeout with diagnostics rather than masking a hang. Gate rollout on repeated successful minimal all-reduces and an application-level correctness check (not merely process exit), then test the real workload. Roll back to the last known-good launcher, interface, or world size if any rank errors, collective mismatch, data corruption, repeated timeout, or performance/SLO regression occurs. Record evidence and assumptions for any platform-specific conclusion.
